It is the third face of the same principle: ברכה = רוח החיה באופנים = נשאת ונושאת.

additions.reason: The Merkavah (divine chariot) is the primary paradigm example of נשאת ונושאת in the Torah: 'כְּגוֹן הַמֶּרְכָּבָה, שֶׁהִיא נִשֵּׂאת וְנוֹשֵׂאת'. The Zohar passage cited identifies it as the prototype of things that are simultaneously carried and carry. It belongs to Package 1 as another face of the נשאת ונושאת principle — it IS what that principle means.

The Holy Ark is cited as the second paradigm of נשאת ונושאת: it was carried by the Levites, yet it carried its carriers. The text says 'וְכֵן הָאָרוֹן, שֶׁהָיוּ נוֹשְאִים אוֹתוֹ וְהוּא נָשָׂא אֶת נוֹשְׂאָיו'. This is the same essential nature as ברכה and נשאת ונושאת — a thing that simultaneously carries and is carried.
additions.source_quote: וְכֵן הָאָרוֹן, שֶׁהָיוּ נוֹשְאִים אוֹתוֹ וְהוּא נָשָׂא אֶת נוֹשְׂאָיו

analysis_notes.notes: Torah LM2:69 is an extremely short Torah (4 sentences) with minimal dataset coverage — only 1 bechina edge. The Torah's argument is compact: the custom of giving a blessing (ברכה) to a drink-carrier is grounded in the Zohar principle of נשאת ונושאת, exemplified by the Merkavah and the Ark. All three example-concepts (כי רוח החיה באופנים, מרכבה, ארון) are absent from the dataset but are explicitly invoked with bechina language as illustrations of the same principle. The final parenthetical remark — that the drink can either break (שברים) from causing cooling and heating — is noted by the Rebbe as unexplained ('לא בֵּאֵר הַדָּבָר הַזֶּה כְּלָל') and introduces no additional bechina relationships.
